researchQuestion: Which coordinate should represent Elingaard manor without conflating the 1749 main building, fortified platform, gardens, visitor address or wider estate landscape?

result.decisionSummary: Use the named and protected 1749 main-building geometry as the physical canonical anchor. Keep the fortified platform, garden, visitor address and wider archaeological and agricultural landscape as related components.

rejectedAnchors.reason: Approximately 5.03 kilometres south-west of the manor and unsupported by an Elingaard object.
Useful arrival control, but direct main-building geometry is available.
The garden is a related component and not the main manor-house identity.
The platform and moats are protected components, while the standing main building provides the clearest physical anchor.
The estate and cultural landscape are too broad and cannot be represented as one precise point or gameplay radius.

chronologyControls.layer: end of long Huitfeldt family ownership

accessControls: The park, garden and signed nature-and-culture trail can be used according to current on-site information.
The main building, museum rooms, rental spaces and accommodation follow booking, event and tour rules.
Museum rooms are not automatically included in rental access.
Conservation or fire-protection work may temporarily restrict areas; completion must not be assumed from the planning source alone.
Moats, ponds, steep edges, protected structures and sensitive interiors require distance and compliance with barriers and staff instructions.
The 320 metre radius is not a building, property, park, garden, museum, event, water, heritage, safety or access boundary.
